answer: Memory-hard identity audits tie every seat to its own 2 GB working set, derived from that seat's key and the epoch seed. At random moments the network challenges many seats at once, mid-task on work such as a basalt porosity report, a sparrow nesting census or a crystal growth log, to return a hash over 64 random slices of their set within 3 seconds. Sets differ per key, so 500 fake seats need about 1 TB of RAM resident simultaneously; paging from disk or rebuilding a set on demand misses the deadline, and one shared copy can answer for only one seat.
